in_hebrew.name: יוחנה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יוחנה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'האל יוחנן' או 'אלוהים הוא חנן'. השם נגזר מהמילה העברית 'חנן', שפירושו 'לרחם' או 'לדאוג'. השם יוחנה מופיע בתנ'ך כהשם של מספר דמויות, בהן יוחנן הכהן ויוחנן בן קורח.

in_greek.name: Ιωάνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιωάνα είναι το ελληνικό ισοδύναμο του εβραϊκού ονόματος יוחנה (Yohanan). Αυτό σημαίνει 'Θεός ελεήμων' (Θεός ελεήμων) ή 'Θεός είναι χαριτόω' (Θεός είναι χαριτόω), που σημαίνει ότι ο Θεός είναι ένα δωρητής χάριτος ή ελέους. Στο Καινή Διαθήκη, η Ιωάνα αναφέρεται ως η μητέρα του Ιωάννη του Βαπτιστού και ως μία από τις πιστές γυναίκες που ακολουθούσαν τον Ιησού.

in_latin.name: Yohana
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Yohana derivatur ex hebraeo נוח (yôḥānān), quod significat 'Deus est miserator' vel 'Deus donat'. Nomen hoc in Ecclesia primitiva christiana usitatum est, praesertim in contextu Ioannis Baptistae et Ioannis Evangelistae, qui ambo in Novum Testamentum inducuntur.

in_english.name: Yohana
in_english.meaning: God is gracious, God is merciful
in_english.long_meaning: The name Yohana originates from the Hebrew name יוחנה (Yohanan), which means 'God is gracious' or 'God is merciful'. It is derived from the Hebrew words 'yochanan', meaning 'God will show favor' or 'God will pardon'. In Christian tradition, Yohana is associated with John the Baptist and John the Apostle, prominent figures in the New Testament. The name has been adopted across various Christian cultures, symbolizing divine favor and mercy.

data.cultural_impact: The name Yohana (also spelled Johana or Joan) has its roots in Hebrew and Aramaic, with the meaning "God is gracious" or "Yahweh is gracious." This name has been popular among Christians, particularly in the Middle East and Europe, and has been borne by numerous saints throughout history. Yohana is a common name among Syriac and Malankara Orthodox Christians.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Yohana holds deep spiritual significance for Christians, reminding us of the boundless grace and kindness of God. This name invites us to reflect on the ways in which God has been gracious to us and shows us how to extend that grace to others. It is a reminder that we are called to live our lives in a manner that mirrors God's generosity and compassion. By carrying the name Yohana, one is invited to embody the spirit of kindness, compassion, and love that came down from God.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament, the name 'John' is a translation of the original Greek name 'Ioannes', which means 'God is gracious'. The Gospel of John, one of the four canonical gospels in the New Testament, is attributed to this apostle named John, who was a close disciple of Jesus.

In the Syriac-speaking Christian tradition, the name 'Yohana' is a transliteration of the Greek name 'Ioannes'.
